[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Universal Functions (ufuncs) and Methods in NumPy"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Universal functions, commonly known as ufuncs, are foundational to NumPy's high performance. They operate element-by-element on ndarray objects, supporting vectorized wrapping of basic arithmetic, trigonometric, and logical operations."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Introduction to Ufuncs"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Unlike standard Python loops, ufuncs are implemented in compiled C code, allowing them to execute operations magnitudes faster. They automatically handle broadcasting, type casting, and other core features."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"import numpy as np

a = np.array([1, 2, 3, 4])
b = np.array([10, 20, 30, 40])

# Vectorized addition using the add ufunc
result = np.add(a, b)
print(result)"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Core Built-in Ufunc Methods"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"All NumPy ufuncs share a set of extremely useful methods that give you deep control over how the operations are executed. These methods include reduce, accumulate, outer, and at."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"reduce(a): Applies the ufunc along a specified axis, reducing the dimension by one."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"accumulate(a): Calculates the accumulated result of the operation over all elements along an axis."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"outer(a, b): Applies the ufunc to all possible pairs of elements from a and b."},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Demonstrating Ufunc Methods"},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"# Using reduce to sum an array
arr = np.array([1, 2, 3, 5])
total = np.add.reduce(arr)
print("Reduced sum:", total)

# Using accumulate to find running totals
running_sum = np.add.accumulate(arr)
print("Accumulated sums:", running_sum)

# Using outer for a multiplication table
row = np.array([1, 2, 3])
col = np.array([10, 20, 30])
table = np.multiply.outer(row, col)
print("Outer product table:")
print(table)"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Mastering ufuncs and their built-in methods is essential for writing efficient, idiomatic NumPy code. By replacing explicit Python iteration with vectorized ufunc operations, you ensure optimal memory usage and execution speed."}]
